newsitem.title: USA: Intel to cut Pentium chip prices later this month.
newsitem.headline: Intel to cut Pentium chip prices later this month.

text.p: Intel Corp., facing strong challenges from smaller rivals, will cut prices of its Pentium computer chip by the end of the month.
The world's biggest chipmaker for years has cut its prices on a schedule about once a quarter. This time, though, the April reductions will be deeper than usual, some analysts speculated.
Major computer makers, such as Compaq Computer Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co, are looking at speedy and cheap chips from rivals Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Cyrix Corp..

Intel spokesman Howard High said the Santa Clara, Calif., company will cut Pentium prices by the end of the month, but declined to say by how much. In the past year, Intel's cuts have ranged up to 25 percent on mainstream chips, which cost about $150.

Intel for years has had no pressure to cut prices. The company's microprocessors handle the basic functions of 90 percent of the world's PCs. It cuts prices regularly as part of its long-term strategy to help the PC market to grow.
But this year, AMD and Cyrix, long the also-rans of the computer chip business, introduced chips that are attractive alternatives for computer makers to the Pentium.

Last week, AMD, based five miles away from Intel, unveiled the K6 -- a microprocessor that crunches numbers and handles graphics as fast as Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro chip, but 25 percent cheaper.

And two months ago, Cyrix, based in Richardson, Texas, introduced a relatively speedy, but bargain-priced, microprocessor for PC makers planning less-than-$1,000 machines. Compaq, the world's biggest PC company, signed up as a customer.

Analysts said AMD and Cyrix do not pose a serious threat to Intel. But Intel's management, as CEO Andy Grove boasted in his recent book, is paranoid. The company could cut prices more deeply than usual, analysts said.
Concerns about the price reductions pushed Intel's stock down Thursday, analysts said. Its shares fell $5 to $137.25.
Stocks of Intel's competitors followed. AMD fell $1.875 to $39.625, while Cyrix fell 75 cents to $19.50.
